Definition: Human-facing manager for integrating deterministic specialist software with Chirality governed agent and filesystem framework.
Notes: Role name; not the same as a domain engine application.

Synonyms: domain engine application; specialist deterministic software
Definition: Specialist deterministic software that owns domain-specific models, calculations, validation, and native workflows.
Structured configuration declaring artifact classes, protected paths, agent-writable paths, deterministic tools, and human gates.
Deterministic CLI or API surface exposed by a domain engine and callable by Chirality under profile constraints.
File or folder that represents domain truth owned by the domain engine.
Manifest, summary, warning list, assumption register, delta table, checklist, or report fragment safe for agents to read and cite.
Proposal, review note, TBD register, draft report section, checklist, dependency note, or reconciliation note permitted by profile.
Path agents must not directly modify.
Write produced by a declared domain tool rather than raw agent file mutation.
Structured proposed model or domain change; not accepted truth until validated and human-approved.

Synonyms: external prover comments; external validation record
Definition: Human-supplied or tool-supplied evidence from an external professional validation workflow.
Required language preventing false claims of professional approval, code compliance, certification, sealing, or external validation.
User manually exports domain summaries or manifests; Chirality agents read and organize them.
Chirality invokes read-only deterministic tools such as validate, summarize, or list states and runs.
Chirality requests domain-generated outputs such as runs, comparisons, report fragments, or handoff manifests.
Agents write structured proposals; the domain engine validates or previews them; the human accepts or rejects them.
Future support for structured external-result records compared by the domain engine.
Notes: Integration level 4; future only unless separately scoped.

Definition: Marker used when missing or ambiguous information must be recorded rather than guessed.
Explicit write targets used to restrict TASK or agent writes.
Scope path that bounds where a dispatched TASK may write when paired with AllowedWriteTargets.
Closure state containing run status, profile state, artifacts read, tools invoked, approvals, blockers, rerun requirements, and next owner.
Record containing profile, integration level, artifacts, tools, human gates, boundary notices, and open issues.
Contract requiring new immutable folders for project-level run, scan, tool-run, boundary review, proposal, or handoff records unless the profile is stricter.
Pointer file that may be updated only to point to the latest accepted snapshot or state record.
Brief shape DOMAIN_ENGINE uses when identifying deterministic tool needs.
Brief shape DOMAIN_ENGINE uses when identifying recurring bounded method needs.
Status value for a profile such as NONE, DRAFT, VALIDATED, ADOPTED, STALE, UNKNOWN, or INVALID depending on context.
Notes: UNKNOWN appears in intake classification; INVALID appears in integration records.

Definition: Decision area owned by the human professional or responsible reviewer, not DOMAIN_ENGINE.
First expected profile and example binding, not the generic ontology.
Requirement that outputs affecting project reasoning exist as project files rather than only in chat.
